question: Plight of Alain‑Claude Bilie‑By‑Nze in Gabon

Alain-Claude Bilie-By-Nze, the former Prime Minister of the Gabonese Republic, was arrested in Libreville on 15 April 2026 and taken into custody the next day after being implicated in a debt case dating back to 2008. His legal representatives have raised questions about the limitation period of this case under Gabonese law.

Bilie-By-Nze, who stood in the April 2025 presidential election, is a leading political figure in Gabon’s post‑transition landscape. Against this background, and given the EU’s interest in strengthening the rule of law and in smooth democratic transitions in central Africa: 1.

Has the Commission been made aware of this matter by its services or the EU Delegation in Libreville? Has it had the opportunity to liaise with the Gabonese authorities on compliance with procedural safeguards in this case?
Via which preferred channels of dialogue will it ensure that Bilie-By-Nze’s right of defence is fully respected, in line with Gabon’s international commitments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.7.2026) The EU Delegation in Libreville and the resident EU Member States Embassies are closely monitoring developments concerning the case of former Prime Minister of the Republic of Gabon and political opponent, Alain-Claude Bilie-By-Nze and are regularly reporting to their respective headquarters.

Since his arrest, the EU has met with representatives of his party, Ensemble pour le Gabon, members of his family and members of the Gabonese civil society to discuss his case. Human rights issues are regularly raised with the Gabonese authorities, most recently during the EU-Gabon Partnership Dialogue on 8 June 20261.

During this dialogue, the EU conveyed concerns regarding arbitrary detentions and other human rights issues, referring also to the perceptions of international Non-Governmental Organisations and the reputational consequences for the country. The EU will continue engaging with the Gabonese authorities on human rights issues, including alleged cases of arbitrary detention and the right of due process.
